activities.caption: drop the marker on the carbonyl dip
activities.name: spCarbonylPlace

config.prompt: The C=O stretch sings near what wavenumber? Place the marker on the IR scale:
config.why: Near 1750 cm⁻¹ — a clean, deep cut. Position tells you which bond; the broad O–H dip near 3300 tells you its situation: this spectrum is basically vinegar introducing itself.

activities.caption: file the isotope doublets
activities.name: spIsotopeBuckets

config.prompt: Isotope patterns are instant element detection. File each signature:

items.label: a peak split into a 3:1 doublet
a peak split into a 1:1 pair

config.why: And high-resolution MS distinguishes 27.9949 (carbon monoxide) from 28.0062 (nitrogen) — eight decimal places apart — which is how breathalysers and sports drug testing work.

activities.anchor: Three further pieces of information make the map complete
activities.caption: stack the NMR reading order
activities.name: spNmrOrder

config.prompt: Reading an NMR map — put the three clues in working order:
items: Chemical shift — where the resonance sits relative to TMS, reporting the electronic neighbourhood
Integral — counting the hydrogens in each group
Splitting — the n+1 rule, counting nearest non-equivalent neighbours
Coupling patterns — linking the groups to each other, as the triplet/quartet pairing does in ethanol
config.why: Hydrogens on carbons next to oxygen resonate downfield near 3–4 ppm; plain alkyl hydrogens near 1 ppm; aldehyde hydrogens near 10.

activities.anchor: The n+1 rule counts only the
activities.caption: one line of the ethanol NMR reading is wrong
activities.name: spNmrSpot

config.prompt: One line of this ethanol NMR summary is wrong. Find it.
lines: Ethanol's ¹H NMR shows three signals: CH₃, CH₂ and OH
The CH₃ peak appears as a triplet of 3 units at ~1.2 ppm
The CH₂ peak appears as a quartet of 2 units at ~3.7 ppm
The CH₃ signal is split by all seven other hydrogens into an eight-line multiplet
The triplet/quartet pairing proves the CH₃ and CH₂ groups are bonded to each other
config.correction: The n+1 rule counts only the nearest non-equivalent neighbours — the CH₃ protons feel their two CH₂ neighbours, hence a triplet.
config.why: Coupling through bonds falls off rapidly with distance, and equivalent protons do not split each other at all.

config.prompt: Copper X-rays (λ = 0.154 nm) hit planes 0.2 nm apart. Roughly what angle does the first-order reflection sit at?
config.why: sin θ = 0.154/0.4 = 0.385, so θ ≈ 23° — the arithmetic a diffractometer runs automatically, turning spot angles into distances between atomic planes.
config.context: Collecting thousands of reflections reconstructs the electron density — the molecule in three dimensions, atoms placed directly.

activities.anchor: a spot at 4.2 cm with the front
activities.caption: fill the blanks — chromatography and wet tests
activities.name: spChromaCloze

config.text: Chromatography reports each spot as an Rf value: a spot at 4.2 cm with the solvent front at 7.0 cm has Rf = %%0%%. The wet tests close the loop: CO₂ turns limewater %%1%%, H₂ pops with a lit splint, and O₂ relights a %%2%% one.
config.hint: Rf is distance moved by spot divided by distance moved by solvent.

activities.anchor: Every structure determination begins with a pure sample
activities.caption: run the purification decision tree
activities.name: spPurifyBranch

config.root: Purity is bought with the right separation — the tree runs on the property that differs. Choose for each sample.

start.text: A crude solid with small amounts of soluble impurities. Which separation?

choices.label: Recrystallisation — dissolve hot, cool, crystallise
choices.feedback: The classic: the desired compound crystallises while the small impurity load stays dissolved — judged by melting-point sharpness.

choices.label: Simple distillation
choices.feedback: That separates liquids by boiling point — the solid never boils.

recryst.text: Now two liquids: ethanol at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. Which separation?

choices.label: Simple distillation
choices.feedback: Right for liquids far apart — though azeotropes cap ethanol's purity near 96 per cent.

choices.label: Paper chromatography
choices.feedback: Chromatography separates by affinity and volatility at tiny scale — not the industrial route for bulk liquids.

distil.text: Last sample: a non-volatile, drug-scale molecule in solution. Which analysis?

choices.label: HPLC — high-pressure liquid chromatography
choices.feedback: Built for non-volatile molecules under pressure — and run the outlet into a mass spectrometer and separation plus identification happen in one instrument.

choices.label: Gas chromatography
choices.feedback: GC needs volatility — this molecule never becomes a gas intact.

hplc.text: Separation chosen, purity verified — melting point, TLC single spot, a clean NMR.

wrong1.text: Back to the tree: pick the property that actually differs.

wrong2.text: Back to the tree: boiling point is the differing property here.

wrong3.text: Back to the tree: volatility is the property GC runs on.

config.why: An unverified yield is a guess with arithmetic on it — purity checks are part of the method, not an afterthought.
